scores.evidence: Redact PII and card numbers (Luhn-valid PANs) before the LLM call and before logging.
scores.rationale: Technical claims (hybrid pgvector, blue/green alias, rule-of-three bound, executor-enforced tool) are accurate; minor imprecision such as 99.7% series cap and 'Claude through Bedrock' has no design consequence.

scores.evidence: It answers customer questions only from published help-center articles, with citations, and hands off to a human agent when it can't answer.
scores.rationale: Resolves the ambiguity by scoping to public docs and explicitly defers account data and logged-in content with reasons; buildable with a small team.

scores.evidence: Visibility checked at ingest and filtered again at query time
scores.rationale: Consistent design with clear ownership; minor loose ends such as Phase 1 handoff ticket depending on ticketing credentials and 'blocked from being deployed (Phase 1)' while Phase 0 uses only staff.

scores.evidence: zero in 100 bounds the rate at ≤ 3% at 95% confidence, so canary review continues
scores.rationale: Risk-specific gates V0–V5 run early, with thresholds labeled ASSUMPTION, blind SME grading, probe sets, canary vs control and continuing production review.

scores.evidence: UNKNOWN: peak chats per hour comes from support ops, needed before the Phase 4 load test
scores.rationale: Assumptions and unknowns are labeled, ranked by plan-changing impact, with the revisit triggers and the way each is confirmed.

scores.evidence: an injected LLM timeout shows the fallback message and fires an alert
scores.rationale: Covers injection, hallucinated commitments, stale/deleted content, outages, abuse/cost runaway, PII, feedback poisoning and partial failures with detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: Rollback means redeploying the previous image through the pipeline. The flag off removes the widget.
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, traces, SLIs, on-call runbook and alias-swap are concrete; ownership and incident response names are thin and the SLO is deferred.

scores.evidence: AI inference cost (per conversation) | — | UNKNOWN: human cost per ticket comes from the support lead
scores.rationale: Cost drivers, caps, kill switch and buy-vs-build check are present, but no per-conversation estimate or basis is given and the budget is left unknown.

scores.evidence: R3: an internal article shown to the public can't be un-shown
scores.rationale: Each decision has a reversibility rating, validation and revisit trigger; model interface, index_version and vendor-neutral eval sets isolate lock-in.

scores.evidence: One service, one ingestion worker, one Postgres with pgvector; no self-hosted model
scores.rationale: Simple fixed chain, no agents, and heavy items deferred; some overhead (six phases, 2-week agent-assist, commitment detector, fallback model, pen test) is heavy for a small team.

scores.evidence: Exit check V0 ... a real request succeeds with one trace across every tier; one deploy and one rollback go through the pipeline
scores.rationale: Thin-slice first, dependency-justified phases, concrete tasks, checkable exit criteria and failure responses for each gate.

checklist.evidence: unpublished or deleted articles gone in ≤ 15 min ... Webhook-driven incremental sync, deletions prioritized, plus a nightly full reconcile.
Section-level chunks carrying article ID, anchor, locale, visibility, updated_at, index_version.
≥ 200 labeled real questions per index version ... Eval report per index_version in CI artifacts
If verification fails, the bot abstains and hands off.
It creates a ticket with the redacted transcript, and a "talk to a human" button works even if the LLM is down.
The handoff call is the only tool. The executor, not the model, enforces it, and its only argument is the session ID.
Only published, public articles; no community posts or comments. Visibility checked at ingest and filtered again at query time
Transcripts kept 30 days (ASSUMPTION, DPO to confirm). Never train on transcripts
It does not read customer account data, and its only action is handing the conversation to a human.
Daily review of a redacted transcript sample ... content-gap reports go to the docs team.
Hard caps: 4k input / 512 output tokens per turn, 5 turns per session, and a provider-account spend limit.

traps.evidence: Every answer must be grounded in a cited article.
Visibility checked at ingest and filtered again at query time
Eval report per index_version in CI artifacts

note: Exceptionally rigorous, well-scoped plan; weakest on concrete cost estimation and some process heaviness, with no listed traps hit.
